items.title: Can you still tell AI-generated text apart in your own language?
items.raw_excerpt: I'm Japanese, and I can still usually spot AI-generated Japanese by its word choice. Some words, like 実務 (practical work) and 帳簿 (a ledger), turn up far more often than they should. Casual ones like 効く (to work well, to be effective) and 刺さる (to pierce > to resonate, to hit home) get used where another word would normally be the first choice. They're the Japanese equivalent of "delve." I'm not a native English speaker, but my impression is that AI-generated English has improved a lot recently and is harder to pick out than it used to be. excerpt_i18n.es: Recientemente, Tang Kai, presidente de la división de ingeniería de software de OPPO, asistió a la Conferencia de Socios del Ecosistema de IA de Alipay. Durante el evento, Tang Kai señaló que una contradicción estructural en el desarrollo actual de los agentes es que la capacidad de los modelos ya ha superado la capacidad organizativa de la cadena industrial. «Hoy en día, no es difícil crear un producto de agente orientado al consumidor con una buena experiencia basada en modelos, pero no es fácil lograr un verdadero ciclo comercial cerrado», afirmó. Tang Kai añadió que los agentes deben comprender mejor a los usuarios, completar más tareas reales y requerir el acceso a servicios y herramientas abundantes para ofrecer una mejor experiencia. Sin embargo, en la industria actual todavía existen numerosos servicios y ecosistemas aislados.
excerpt_i18n.en:
Recently, Tang Kai, President of OPPO's Software Engineering Business Unit, attended the Alipay AI Ecosystem Partner Conference. At the conference, Tang Kai stated that a structural contradiction in the current development of Agents is that model capabilities have outpaced the organizational capabilities of the industry chain. "Today, building a To C Agent product with a good experience based on models is no longer difficult, but forming a real business closed loop is not easy." Tang Kai said that Agents need to better understand users, complete more real tasks, and call on rich services and tools to provide users with a better experience. However, the industry still has a large number of isolated services and ecosystem islands.  

Tang Kai, President of OPPO's Software Engineering Business Unit — Agent Industry Collaboration: A Global Catch-Up for AI  

At the end of 2024, Anthropic launched MCP, attempting to solve the connection problem between AI applications and external data and tools through open protocols. In 2025, Google launched the A2A protocol, providing a solution for Agents developed by different vendors and frameworks to communicate and collaborate with each other. By April 2026, A2A had gained support from more than 150 institutions and entered multiple mainstream cloud platforms.  

From "Agent connecting to tools" (MCP) to "Agent connecting to Agents" (A2A), the evolution of industry infrastructure points to the same question: as models become smarter, how to integrate fragmented demands, services, and industrial capabilities truly.

On August 10, Nvidia announced it would join forces with six major Wall Street financial institutions to establish a series of independent computing power financing platforms, with plans to gradually mobilize more than $500 billion in third-party capital. The collaboration targets the funding bottleneck in the GPU sales chain—if customers cannot borrow money, even surging computing demand will struggle to translate into actual orders. But why now? How will this financing machine work? And if computing power revenue falls short of debt obligations and GPU residual values come in below expectations, who ultimately bears the risk?

01 Five-year contracts underpin GPU loans, but short-term customers are shut out

According to SemiAnalysis estimates, AI-related debt balances will exceed $7 trillion by 2029, second only to the U.S. residential mortgage financing market at roughly $13 trillion. Online documents, WeCom, clock-ins and approvals— tools kept changing, seemingly transforming office workflows, yet the time actually freed up never seemed to shrink. Look at the elevator ads around you: on one side is WorkBuddy, on the other Doubao and Qianwen. Even airport lounges are saturated with AI office scenarios. When all players crowd into the same track, do office software products offer just more AI features, or do they reconstruct the way we work? excerpt_i18n.es: Desde hace diez años, los gigantes tecnológicos de internet han intentado ayudar a los trabajadores a mejorar su eficiencia. Documentos en línea, WeChat empresarial, fichajes y aprobaciones: las herramientas no han dejado de cambiar y parece que la forma de trabajar en la oficina ha cambiado con ellas, pero el tiempo realmente liberado no parece haber disminuido. Hasta que, diez años después, los grandes modelos y los agentes han hecho que las cosas mejoren: la IA puede recopilar información por sí sola, utilizar herramientas y descomponer tareas, y el software de oficina ha empezado a trabajar de verdad por la gente.
